The new code uses `rv != dash`, so `is_dash` is true for every non-dash value and false for an actual "-". With allow_dash=True, normal paths will skip resolve_path, exists and the other checks, and "-" will be validated as a filesystem path. It should be `rv == dash`. import click

def test_dash_passthrough_and_checks(tmp_path):
    t = click.Path(allow_dash=True, exists=True)
    assert t.convert('-', None, None) == '-'
    assert t.convert(b'-', None, None) == b'-'
    import pytest
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter):
        t.convert(str(tmp_path / 'missing'), None, None)

reviews.raw:
The diff has an inverted condition. The old code was `rv in (b"-", "-")`, which is true when the value is a dash. The new code is `rv != dash`, which is true when the value is not a dash. So `is_dash` is now true for every non-dash value and false for a dash value.

With `allow_dash=True`, regular paths would skip resolution and existence checks, while a real "-" would go through them and fail the exists check. That is a clear defect.

The new test does not catch it. It only checks that no BytesWarning is raised, and it never asserts on behavior. The test passes `None` for the ctx and param, and with the inversion the values '' and b'' would not be treated as dash, so they would go through the checks with default exists=False. Nothing fails, so the test misses the bug.

The failing pager tests in test_utils are unrelated.

The test suite at PR head shows 24 failures in test_echo_via_pager, for example "Writing to stderr during generator execution", where the pager output is '' and 'testtest\n' was expected. This is a real regression, or at least a failing test that the PR leaves broken.

Why it likely fails: `_pipepager` now yields `c.stdin` directly, and the wrapper's `close()` only flushes. The previous code detached the TextIOWrapper. The pager process needs EOF to emit its output, and `_pipepager`'s finally presumably closes stdin. But `_PagerWriter` has no `__enter__`/`__exit__`, and `echo` may rely on other stream attributes. The failures happen with `less`, so something in the flow differs.

Whatever the cause, the failing tests exercise the changed code and fail at the PR head, so I'm blocking.

comments.body: get_pager_file wraps `stream.buffer` in a new MaybeStripAnsi (an io.TextIOWrapper) and never detaches it. When the wrapper is garbage collected, TextIOWrapper closes the underlying buffer. In the `_nullpager` path that buffer belongs to the real `sys.stdout`, so using the pager closes stdout. This matches the 189 test errors at the PR head, which fail with `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file`. Call `detach()` on the wrapper in the `finally` block, or avoid wrapping stdout's buffer. Separately, `_pipepager` and `_tempfilepager` no longer fall back to another pager when the command is missing: they yield stdout with color forced to False instead of trying `less` or `more`. A nonexistent `$PAGER` previously fell through to the next pager, so this is a behaviour regression.

comments.body: The new test `test_hide_input_value_never_leaks_when_err_true` calls `runner.invoke(cli, input="leaky\n", mix_stderr=False)`. Click 8.2 and later removed the `mix_stderr` argument from `CliRunner`, and this repo already has `get_pager_file`, so it is a recent version. The call most likely raises `TypeError` before any assertion runs. That would explain the one failure in the suite at the PR head. Even if the argument were accepted, the test asserts only on `leaky` and checks no masked output, so it proves little.

The raw-value pass uses `(?<!\w)` and `(?!\w)`. A value that starts or ends with a non-word character, such as `!pass`, will not be masked when it is glued to a word character (e.g. `abc!pass`), so the value can leak. The old code fell back to a generic message whenever the raw value appeared in the message, so this is a security regression from the previous behavior. The existing test `partial-word-match-falls-back-to-generic` also appears to contradict the new masking behavior.

The `self.allow_dash` check was dropped from `is_dash`. With `allow_dash=False`, a value of '-' now bypasses the exists/file_okay/dir_okay/resolve checks and is returned as-is, whereas before it was validated as an ordinary path (e.g. exists=True would fail). Restore it: `is_dash = self.file_okay and self.allow_dash and rv == dash`.

As a result the route's `status_code` (e.g. `@app.get(..., status_code=201)`) and any status set via the injected `Response` parameter in a dependency are silently ignored, and the response is always 200. def write(self, text: str) -> int:
    if not self.color:
        text = strip_ansi(text)

Either way, 24 existing tests fail on the PR head, and the diff does not update them to expect new behavior. This is a regression and must not be merged.
